factual_methodology.summary: Separates 2026 budget allocations from 2027 proposal and actual expenditure; 2025 observed personnel from 2026/2035 statutory targets; NATO advisory chair from operational command; conditional Russian capability from intent; mandatory questionnaire/medical assessment from actual conscription; announced brigade from fully deployable strength.

contrary_evidence: Breuer explicitly warns of a possible Russian capability to attack NATO from 2029, not a confirmed political decision to do so.
The 2027 €109.7bn plus €29.9bn is a draft budget and does not measure delivered systems, expended funds or deployable formations.
Germany's 2026 service model remains predominantly voluntary; compulsory enlistment would require separate parliamentary action.
German 2025 observed force size of approximately 184,200 is far below 2035 planning ambition; a legal personnel target is not operational readiness.
The 2026 ZMSBw survey finds different levels of support for NATO membership, spending and actual military action; public consent is not a single uniform indicator.
Modern NATO and parliamentary controls differ fundamentally from the political institutions and objectives of Germany's 1914-1945 wars.
limitations: Primary-source verification was targeted to principal current and quantitative claims; not all 25 bibliographic entries were opened independently.

ZMSBw April-May 2026 survey is representative of German-speaking residents aged 16+ in private households with 39% response rate; the report does not extrapolate results to every person or assume willingness to serve.
Military industrial throughput, stockpiles, classified OPLAN details, readiness and future deliveries cannot be independently quantified from the cited public material.
Budget authorization, NATO spending methodology, procurement, delivery and deployment are not interchangeable.
2027-2035 targets and the 2029 Russian capability window are conditional, not observed outcomes or probability estimates.
Strict all-pending editorial-depth CI is red due to unchanged older rejected drafts lacking visual evidence; the approved/published production build and candidate-specific minimums passed.
No independent academic peer review was performed; a passing CI build does not prove live domain deployment.
notes: Independent QA tied to immutable pending and two staged Git blobs, after primary-source spot checks and bilingual visual/source parity verification. publication.selection_rationale: Major evidence-based transformation of German defence expenditure, officer leadership, NATO positioning, service law, permanent Lithuanian basing and whole-of-society logistics in 2026, explained through two world wars, post-1945 constitutional reconstruction and post-1990 demobilisation.

en.title: Germany's Military Awakening: From the First World War to Europe's Strategic Rearmament in 2026
en.deck: A historical and strategic investigation of German rearmament, from Hindenburg and the Wehrmacht to Breuer, Freuding, NATO's eastern flank, mobilisation, defence industry and parliamentary control.
en.regime: German defence has shifted from a limited expeditionary model to territorial and collective deterrence, while the scale of operating readiness lags behind fiscal and legal commitments.

contrary_evidence: Fiscal budgets are authorised or proposed amounts, not receipts of materiel or deployable force; 2027 proposal should not be portrayed as 2027 actual spending.
Breuer's warning that Russia could possess capability to attack from 2029 explicitly does not mean Russia has decided to attack.
NATO Military Committee chair is a collective advisory office, not SACEUR or German command over Allied forces.
2026 military service remains primarily voluntary, with mandatory questionnaires for men and future medical assessment; compulsory enlistment requires further legal steps.
Historical German military aggression does not make contemporary parliamentary NATO defence identical to imperial or Nazi military institutions.
limitations: Budget categories of the national core budget, the Bundeswehr special fund and NATO expenditure ratios are not directly interchangeable.
End-2025 active personnel are observed, while 2026/2035 staffing and end-2027 Lithuanian brigade figures are planned targets.
OPLAN DEU full content remains classified: only public summary and quantified transit scenario can be analysed.
Assessment of Russian military capability from 2029 is a planning scenario, not independent verification of future attack intention.
Industrial throughput, availability of equipment, training and reserve deployability require rolling official confirmation.
Poll findings represent April–May 2026 respondents and vary by question and subgroup.
